title: cast_motion() does not follow rotation
body:
### Tested versions

Tested and found in v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f] and v4.6.1.stable.official [14d19694e] 

### System information

Godot v4.7.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9649) - AMD Ryzen 9 9900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 31.10 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Found it when working on a custom character controller's collision check. When using cast_motion(), it ignores the rotation of the shape's transform and always uses the global basis to calculate rotation. That means that if the object and the casting shape subsequently rotate, the cast is thrown into the wrong direction, not following the rotation of the transform but the global axis instead.
At the same time, the position of the transform is still respected. That means that, though the rotation is wrong, it is cast from the correct place.
I obviously want the rotation of the transform to be respected in the calculation for the cast.

### Steps to reproduce

You need to create a shape, pass it a global transform, and throw it into the PhysicsShapeQueryParameters3D, (all the shapes I tested had the same bug). The cast motion will just ignore the rotation regardless of how you pass the transform (you can create a shape object and reuse it or create a new one every frame).

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Below is the MRP attached. Using WASD, you can move the character in the direction with respect to rotation; using left and right arrow keys, you can rotate, and using space, you can push the character forward regardless of the rotation.
If you were to move without rotating in any direction (except left, which works inconsistently for some reason), you would hit the wall and not move beyond it as expected. But if you were to rotate, it would start pathing through the walls if moved with respect to rotation. But when pushed into the same direction as the world basis, the character will once again detect the walls correctly.
